prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Completely redesign the Elysium environment in image 1, preserving only the handmade painterly engraved medium also seen in image 2. The old scene is rejected because its canyon, stairs, cypresses and central river resemble every other location. Replace its entire composition. Deliver one wide landscape painting, 1536x1024, no labels. Elysium is now a luminous expansive coastal meadow at the edge of the world: rolling emerald and sage grass fills the foreground and middle ground, abundant golden blossoms and flowering fruit trees on the outer thirds, long flowering branches stirred by a gentle sea breeze. A clear turquoise Oceanus and distant small blessed islands appear across the far horizon, with a single modest sunlit tower far away on one island, not a huge classical temple. Warm honey and apricot sunlight, bright pale blue sky, inviting rich spring vegetation. A narrow calm inlet touches the bottom-right corner to imply ferry access, but NO central river, canyon walls, ruined columns, large stone stairs, waterfall, or repeated cypress skyline. Build distinct organic rounded silhouettes and open airy space, natural diagonal path through the meadow. Myth inspiration: Homer's mild Elysian plain and Pindar's island flowers and ocean breezes, interpreted for the game. Keep overall picture atmospheric and tactile, not photoreal or cartoon. Beautiful welcoming place without angels, halos or moral ranking of passengers. No named people, no boat, no UI, text, icons, watermark or decorative border. Put lush detail at edges and keep central meadow relatively simple; do not replace it with empty dark water.

Deliver one wide landscape painting 1536x1024. Discard the old central river, side landing, cypresses, ruins, columns and repeated rocky valley. A few small translucent human shades drift far apart in the middle distance, no identifiable story characters and no horror expressions. Sky is a heavy muted lavender-gray canopy, no sun disc, sunset, mountains, buildings or trees. A narrow still dark water margin touches the very bottom of frame to imply ferry access, but the flowers and fog occupy almost the entire picture. An indistinct worn path disappears straight into the mist slightly off center. Mood: hushed, remote, suspended memory. Myth basis: Homer's meadow of asphodel inhabited by shades. Painted illustrative detail with subtle etched paper grain matching the character style. Strong horizontal plain silhouette, white flowers on gray-violet with minimal amber, sharply different from golden coastal Elysium and dark cliff environments. No text, logos, UI, numbers, labels or border. No temples, aqueduct, waterfalls, moored boat or lantern post.

Use case: stylized-concept. Redesign image 1, the haven, from scratch as a clearly different environment. Image 2 sets painterly engraved style and the bronze lantern. One wide painting, 1536x1024. The camera is INSIDE a low timber boathouse built into a natural rock alcove, looking diagonally across the workshop toward a small side opening onto the misty river at the far right. One long spectral hand reaches out toward the viewer with five clearly formed clawlike fingers, another lower hand clutches torn cloth; keep both hands fully inside the frame. The head and shoulders form a jagged looming silhouette, with shredded black-gray burial fabric whipping outward like smoke. Remnants of pale ivory shroud and recognizable human features preserve the origin as an abandoned soul. Body twists into turbulent cold blue-black vapour, a few faint muted ember cracks through the smoke imply stored anger. Strong directional cold rim light separates silhouette, dark face kept readable. Threat comes from expression, posture and torn spectral shape. No gore, exposed organs, wounds, skull face, demon horns, bat wings, armor, weapon, lantern, crown or background scenery. No text, numbers, UI, logo or border. This is a fantasy game wraith, not a portrait of a named mythological Fury. Keep enough margin around fingers and hood for contain placement. Dramatic, scary and accusatory, not gentle, mournful or sleepy.
